```plato
//==
// # Remeshing
//
// Changing a mesh's TRIANGULATION rather than its shape: refining it, coarsening
// it, regularizing it, and smoothing it. The types the passes hand each other are
// declared in `remeshing.types.plato`, whose header states the one design decision
// everything here follows — every operation is a whole-mesh REBUILD driven by
// decisions taken against a single unchanging input, never an in-place edit.
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Triangle corners
//  - Derived triangle connectivity
//  - Vertex remaps
//  - Welding
//  - Edge split
//  - Edge collapse
//  - Edge flip
//  - Loop and Butterfly subdivision
//  - Catmull-Clark and Doo-Sabin subdivision
//  - The subdivision scheme driver
//  - Smoothing
//  - Quadric error metrics
//  - Quadric decimation
//  - Isotropic remeshing
//
// COST. Nothing in this vocabulary has a keyed container (see LINT013 on `IMap`),
// so an edge table is recovered by scanning corners against corners: building
// `TriangleMeshTopology` is quadratic in the corner count, and that build is the
// price of admission for every pass below. Treat a few thousand triangles as the
// working range and read the per-function notes before sizing an input.

library Remeshing
{
    //==
    // # Triangle corners
    //
    // A triangle mesh's corners are numbered exactly as `CornerTable`
    // (`topology.types.plato`) numbers them: corner c belongs to triangle c / 3 at
    // slot c mod 3. A corner also READS as the directed edge leaving its own
    // vertex for the next corner's vertex, which is what lets the connectivity
    // below be recovered without storing a half-edge record per side.

    // The triangle a corner belongs to: corners come three per face, in face order.
    CornerFace(corner: CornerIndex): FaceIndex
        => FaceIndex(corner.Value / 3);
```
